1.explanation: Both Toggle and ToggleSmall explicitly set aria-label={null} on the <input> and instead attach any aria-label to the <label> element. Screen readers ignore aria-label on a <label> and only read the input’s accessible name. As a result, passing aria-label into the component has no effect. To fix this, the aria-label prop must be forwarded to the <input> element rather than being nulled out, ensuring the input’s accessible name includes the provided string.
1.bug_scenario: In the demo screenshot, the first Toggle (with only labelText) reads correctly as “Bluetooth, unticked, Tick box.” The second Toggle (with labelA, labelB, and an aria-label prop) renders the visible “Bluetooth” text but VoiceOver only announces “Tick box” with no label. In other words, the provided aria-label is never applied to the underlying input, so screen readers don’t pick it up.

2.explanation: In both Toggle.js and ToggleSmall.js the input element explicitly sets aria-label={null}, overriding any aria-label passed in via props. The labeling logic then only applies aria-label on the <label> element (and in Toggle.js that logic skips the aria-label when a string labelText is present). As a result, when consumers supply only labelA/labelB and aria-label (no labelText), the input has no accessible name and the screen reader reads only the default. To fix the bug, the render method in Toggle and the ToggleSmall functional component need to stop nullifying the input’s aria-label and instead pass through the provided aria-label so that assistive technologies can pick it up.
2.bug_scenario: The user provides an aria-label on a Toggle component (especially when using only labelA/labelB without a visible labelText), but VoiceOver does not announce that aria-label. In the screen recording you can see two toggles: the first has a visible labelText so it reads correctly; the second uses labelA/labelB and aria-label, yet VoiceOver only announces "Tick box" (the default) and ignores the passed aria-label.
